purpose: Preserve the decision served, publication status, source location, implementation, and limits of each v0.16.0 formula.

formulas.name: Assessment-state domain
formulas.decision_served: Identify the allowed categorical state for each case-stage proposition.
formulas.plain_language: A stage may be supported, partially supported, unsupported, indeterminate, or outside scope.

source_locations.marker: Let the six required states for case $c$

limitations: The states are categorical and assign no numeric distance.
Outside scope cannot remove a conceptually required event-level stage.

formulas.name: Event-control decision rule
formulas.expression_latex: EventControl(c)=\begin{cases}FAIL,&\exists j\in R:s_{c,j}=U\\UNRESOLVED,&\nexists j\in R:s_{c,j}=U\land\exists j\in R:s_{c,j}\in\{P,I\}\\PASS,&\forall j\in R:s_{c,j}=S\end{cases}
formulas.decision_served: Classify event-level control for a case from its six required stage states.
formulas.plain_language: One unsupported stage produces a fail. A partial or indeterminate stage leaves the result unresolved when no stage fails. Every required stage must be supported for a pass.
limitations: The rule assigns no aggregate control score or case ranking.
The released results apply only to the three purposively selected packets.

formulas.name: Event-control composition
formulas.expression_latex: EventControl=Access\land Comprehension\land Authority\land Feasibility\land Exercise\land Propagation
formulas.decision_served: Expose the six conditions that jointly compose event-level control.
formulas.plain_language: Assigned authority can affect execution only when the full path from information access through execution propagation remains intact.
limitations: This composition is a documentary decision rule, not a causal model.
The compiled v0.16.0 paper states the six-stage logic in prose and the case-level rule rather than displaying this shorthand equation.

formulas.name: Accountable-control composition
formulas.decision_served: Separate event-level control from the institution's later ability to correct the record and repair harm.
formulas.plain_language: Accountable control requires event-level control, correction, and repair.
limitations: A later correction or repair cannot retroactively establish event-level control.
The three released case results classify event-level control only.

formulas.name: Learning-control composition
formulas.decision_served: Separate institutional learning from event-level and post-event accountability claims.
formulas.plain_language: Learning control requires accountable control plus evidence that the institution changed its decision architecture.
limitations: A later reform cannot repair the control conditions in an earlier event.
The formula supplies no estimate of whether a reform reduced later harm.

formulas.name: Intervention-time margin
formulas.decision_served: Define the timing evidence needed to test whether an intervention could reach execution before commitment.
formulas.plain_language: Subtract the time required to interpret, decide, transmit, and propagate an intervention from the time available before commitment.

source_locations.marker: Proposed timing measure for contemporary records

limitations: The three historical packets lack complete timestamps, so the project does not calculate this measure for them.
A nonnegative margin is necessary but does not by itself establish a functioning intervention channel.

formulas.name: Claim-eligibility rule
formulas.decision_served: Determine whether a mapped claim may enter a conclusion.
formulas.plain_language: A claim must be traceable, integrity-checked, human-reviewed, fit for its exact scope, and supported by eligible dependencies.
limitations: Passing the rule establishes internal conclusion eligibility under the declared map.
It does not establish source truth, independent reliability, or external validity.

formulas.name: Documentary evidence-gap indicator
formulas.decision_served: Identify a represented human-control claim that lacks complete substantiation under the event-control procedure.
formulas.plain_language: The indicator is one when a case is represented as human-controlled and its event-control result is fail or unresolved.
limitations: The project has not coded a population of institutional human-control representations.
The indicator does not establish fault, deliberate misrepresentation, legal liability, unsafe outcome, or prevalence.
